summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a suprapubic catheter, was admitted for a right percutaneous nephrolithotomy due to bilateral kidney stones. The procedure was performed without complications, and a temporary nephrostomy tube was placed on the right side. He received intravenous antibiotics for 24 hours and was transitioned to oral pain control with acetaminophen and a narcotic for breakthrough pain. The right nephrostomy tube was clamped and subsequently removed on postoperative day one after he remained pain-free. He tolerated a regular diet, had stable labs, and no signs of infection. He was discharged home with instructions to care for the remaining left nephrostomy tube, continue fosfomycin, monitor for complications, and prepare for the left-sided procedure in the coming weeks.
